title: Apply terminal typography and initial geometry settings
description:
## Outcome

Preserve the non-opacity portion of the former broad presentation-settings plan as a separate later implementation slice. After terminal background opacity is proved, let the accepted Eon caller supply bounded primary monospace family, ordered fallback families, font size, line-height multiplier, and initial columns and rows before Venus creates its window.

This planning issue changes no `VEN-C*` contract. Before code, the user must approve whether this expands `VEN-C11` or creates another stable Venus contract, and that contract must be indexed with the exact Eon compatibility order.

- Consumer: Eon or EonTerm launching one Venus surface.
- Trigger: launch with accepted typed typography and geometry values, or no overrides.
- Result: Venus applies the values through the one authoritative grid consumed by rendering, resize, pointer mapping, selection, accessibility, cursor anchoring, and IME placement. Absence preserves the accepted 16 px, 10 by 18 logical-cell fallback and current geometry.
- Failures: malformed, non-finite, out-of-range, unavailable, or internally inconsistent values fail before the native window is visible and never silently fall back.

Impact: MED/HIGH. Effort: L. Implementation risk: MED/HIGH because text fitting and every geometry consumer meet here. Confidence: HIGH that the outcome is independently schedulable; exact field bounds and contract identity remain intentionally unresolved until approval.

## Evidence

- Closed `ven-0o6` proves the current no-profile 16 logical-pixel text, 10 by 18 logical-cell metrics, shared geometry owner, and native acceptance.
- `src/render.rs` owns `CellMetrics`, font fitting, glyphon buffers, rendering, hit geometry, and initial logical size.
- `src/main.rs`, input, selection, IME, accessibility, and workspace materialization all consume those authoritative metrics.
- The former description of `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` bundled these values with opacity. The user approved splitting opacity into the first vertical slice on 2026-08-14 rather than delaying it behind typography and geometry.

## Scope

In scope:
- One accepted Eon-to-Venus startup boundary for primary family, ordered fallbacks, font size, line height, initial columns, and initial rows.
- Existing `CellMetrics`, font selection/fitting, renderer, resize, input mapping, selection, accessibility, cursor, IME, workspace, launch parsing, focused tests, contract proof, README LOC, and accepted user-visible docs/changelog.
- Exact glyphon 0.12.0 and cosmic-text 0.19.0 behavior already selected by the repository.

Out of scope:
- Background opacity, themes, terminal colors, blur, background images, cursor effects, font packaging, live reload, settings UI, arbitrary split layout, Kitty graphics, renderer replacement, macOS support promise, or Orbit protocol changes.
- A generic profile framework, Venus config file, environment-variable-per-setting boundary, or second geometry owner.

## Implementation notes

1. Wait for `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` to prove the minimal launch/configuration boundary and avoid overlapping its launch/renderer work.
2. Reread all current metric, font, renderer, workspace, input, selection, accessibility, cursor, resize, and IME owners plus the accepted opacity contract.
3. Obtain user approval for the exact contract id, field names, types, bounds, missing-font behavior, and Eon/Venus update order; index it before code.
4. Extend the existing launch boundary directly. Keep `CellMetrics` and the existing font fitter as the sole geometry and typeface owners.
5. Use TDD for pure bounds, scale-factor geometry, fallback ordering, and invalid profiles, then native Linux dogfood for text quality and configured availability.
6. Add no dependency unless the repository crate gate proves existing glyphon/cosmic-text and platform font facilities insufficient and the user approves the choice.
7. Follow the immutable source candidate then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

## Acceptance

- No-profile behavior is identical to the accepted current defaults.
- Primary family and ordered fallbacks resolve deterministically; unavailable required values fail with bounded diagnostics under the approved policy.
- Font size and line height derive one coherent cell grid at scale factors 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, and 2.0.
- Initial columns and rows produce the requested authoritative grid subject only to explicit native size limits.
- Rendering, resize, hit testing, wheel normalization, selection, cursor, IME, accessibility, and workspace materialization consume the same metrics without drift.
- Native Linux proof covers default and configured Latin, Unicode, wide/combining text, Nerd Font symbols, regular/bold/italic, box/Braille, resize, selection, cursor, IME, accessibility, standalone, and workspace paths.
- Exact locked Rust checks, contract proof, docs, LOC accounting, and `git diff --check` pass on one immutable candidate.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

Focused tests must prove defaults, bounds, fallback ordering, missing-font policy, all named scale factors, initial geometry, and shared consumer geometry.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until the exact contract and compatibility order are user-approved and indexed.
- Stop before a dependency, manifest edit, font package, second metric owner, generic profile framework, live watcher, renderer replacement, or Orbit/Eon workspace protocol change.
- Stop if another active issue owns the same launch, CellMetrics, font, renderer, input geometry, accessibility, or IME surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

This issue deliberately excludes opacity. Expand it only for another user-approved typography or initial-geometry field. Broader Mars parity remains a Nova product decision.

title: Allow callers to disable native window decorations
description:
## Why

Venus always requests a decorated native window, so users cannot opt out of the desktop title bar even when Eon already provides its own workspace chrome. The user chose an explicit way to disable the native window bar, not a new undecorated default.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a direct Venus launcher or an Eon composition that supplies Venus launch arguments.
- Trigger: launch Venus with an explicit no-decorations option.
- Result: Venus requests an undecorated native window before creation. Without the option, the existing decorated default is unchanged.
- Invalid options fail immediately with bounded usage text before any window or transport is created.
- The first proof is Linux Wayland/X11. Other platforms remain architecture targets and may follow exact winit behavior until separately proved.

Contract routing:
- Add one user-approved VEN-C9 launch/presentation contract before implementation because the option is a new consumer-visible surface.
- Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, every Orbit/Eon protocol, native content geometry, and lifecycle.
- This Venus Bead supplies only the native capability. A persistent Eon product setting is owned by Eon and requires separate Eon planning; do not create a Venus settings system.

## Evidence

- `src/main.rs:118-129` creates `Window::default_attributes()` without overriding decorations, so exact winit 0.30.13 keeps its `true` default.
- `src/main.rs:1048-1055` accepts only zero, one, or two positional socket arguments and has no launch option.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 `src/window.rs:350-358` provides `WindowAttributes::with_decorations(bool)`; `src/window.rs:1150-1168` documents server- or winit-provided decorations and the decorated default.
- Exact winit Wayland support requests and hides client/server decorations through the existing backend; X11 uses the existing Motif decoration hint. No new dependency or custom titlebar is required.
- `README.md:89-96` records configuration and settings as outside the current slice, so the minimum Venus-owned surface is a launch option rather than a config file.

Impact: MED for focused and tiling-window workflows.
Effort: S.
Implementation risk: MED because undecorated windows intentionally lose native title-bar close and drag affordances.
Confidence: HIGH for the native capability and MED for later Eon configuration UX.

## Scope

In scope:
- Minimal launch-option parsing in `src/main.rs` using existing standard-library argument handling.
- Apply the chosen boolean through exact winit `WindowAttributes::with_decorations` before window creation.
- Focused parsing/default tests, bounded usage text, README run documentation, new VEN-C9 contract/proof, and LOC accounting.
- Native Linux Wayland dogfood; X11 dogfood when available.

Out of scope:
- Changing the default; runtime toggling; custom client-side titlebars; new close, drag, maximize, or minimize controls; keyboard shortcuts; persistence; a Venus config file; or a CLI parsing dependency.
- Eon config-schema or launcher changes, window transparency, fullscreen, size, position, theme, tab/pane chrome, macOS implementation, or protocol changes.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `src/main.rs` window and argument owners, README run surface, contracts, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 `WindowAttributes::with_decorations`, `Window::set_decorations`, Wayland decoration, and X11 decoration-hint implementations.

Comparison only:
- Current desktop environment behavior for decorated and undecorated Eon windows. No external terminal implementation is needed for this one native capability.

Rejected:
- Permanently removing decorations, building an Eon-owned titlebar first, runtime decoration toggles, environment-variable policy, a general settings framework, or adding a CLI parser crate for one boolean.

Platform classification:
- Isolated platform dependency. Winit owns the native request. Linux is proved first; macOS feasibility is preserved but runtime behavior remains unproved.

## Acceptance and Verification

- Launch with no decoration option produces the same decorated request as today.
- The explicit option produces a window created with decorations disabled.
- The option works with the default socket and both accepted positional socket forms.
- Unknown options and excess positional arguments fail before window creation with current, deterministic usage text.
- Existing socket paths, Wayland application identity, accessibility adapter, renderer initialization, IME, resize, close handling, and workspace/Orbit behavior remain unchanged.
- No dependency, config file, runtime toggle, or custom window control is added.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native Wayland dogfood verifies decorated default and explicit borderless launch. Verify X11 when available and record any window-manager hint limitation.
- Promote VEN-C9 only against the exact proof-bearing commit; retain all consumed Eon and Orbit revisions.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for user choice if a complete useful result requires a persistent Eon setting rather than the bounded Venus launch capability.
- Stop if a supported Linux backend cannot honor the request through existing winit without custom decorations.
- Stop before adding replacement close/drag controls, a settings owner, another dependency, or cross-repository implementation.
- Stop if source or proof revisions drift materially before implementation.

## Maintenance Notes

The default stays decorated because it preserves native close and drag affordances. Borderless mode is an explicit opt-in and may rely on desktop shortcuts for movement and closure. Add Eon configuration only in an Eon-owned follow-up after the launch capability proves useful.

title: Render one accepted Orbit session in a minimum Linux window
description: Implement the smallest Venus slice: one Linux window consumes canonical structured frames from an already-running Orbit session, renders their accepted rich state, sends semantic input and resize, remains transient across client exit, and explains bounded attachment or server failure.
design:
Begin only after the user activates Venus, accepts the backend and composition decision, and accepts one exact-revision canonical Orbit protocol-consumption shape. Pin the exact accepted Orbit commit and ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states. Decode accepted ORBF v1 complete frames into one persistent Venus PresentationState before producing draw inputs; reconnect and resync replace that state coherently. This keeps a later user-approved patch protocol compatible with the same reducer model without implementing patches now.

Before manual window dogfood, use a bounded canonical frame corpus or the smallest protocol-faithful source to prove deterministic decode and frame-to-draw inputs without a live PTY, handwritten mirror schema, raw VT parser, or second terminal authority. Keep Linux window and GPU mechanics inside Venus and report any protocol gap to Orbit through separate owner commits and compatibility sequencing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user activates Venus, Orbit orb-9o6 is closed, and the accepted protocol-consumption plus backend and composition decisions are recorded before implementation.
2. The Execution baseline records the exact Orbit proof commit, consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states, affected VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 contracts, intended surfaces, and pre-existing worktree state.
3. The pre-code Reference gate and accepted Crate gate satisfy AGENTS.md; manifest changes match the user-approved protocol and dependency shapes exactly.
4. A focused nonvisual check consumes canonical Orbit ORBF v1 frames, applies complete frames and ordered revisions to one bounded persistent PresentationState, and deterministically produces draw inputs for styled Unicode and graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, reconnect, and failure cases.
5. One Linux window attaches to an already-running Orbit session, renders coherent current state, and sends semantic keyboard input and resize through Orbit.
6. Closing or crashing Venus leaves Orbit and the PTY alive; reopening receives and applies coherent current state.
7. Attach rejection, incompatible or invalid frames, revision failures, and Orbit loss produce clear bounded failures rather than hangs or invented state.
8. Venus owns no PTY, terminal emulator, terminal-query response, raw VT parser, mirrored protocol schema, terminal history content, workspace topology, or Eon policy.
9. Closure records deterministic checks, manual visual dogfood, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, exact Orbit compatibility, proof revisions, and remaining gaps.
10. Patches, history pages, ordered terminal effects, richer resources, tabs, panes, sidebars, popups, settings, visual effects, configuration, plugins, remote or web access, macOS implementation, packaging, and distribution remain excluded.
notes: Required references and classifications are in docs/REFERENCES.md. Orbit orb-bi4.4 is the cross-repository acceptance tracker; this Bead is the sole owner of Venus implementation. A required new Orbit trace format, command, package, adapter, or compatibility window returns for explicit user choice.

title: Recover the selected Orbit attachment after transient loss
description:
## Contract routing

Change and harden user-approved `VEN-C3` so an already-open Venus client automatically retries its selected Orbit endpoint after a retryable local transport loss. Harden `VEN-C4` by retaining an explicit bounded failure during backoff and reconnecting state during an attempt. Preserve `VEN-C1`, `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C7`, and `VEN-C8`; in particular, an unchanged Eon workspace snapshot remains a complete no-op and never triggers Orbit work.

Consume Orbit `ORB-C1`, `ORB-C3`, `ORB-C4`, and `ORB-C7`, canonical ORBS v2, and `orbit-protocol` 0.1.0 at exact accepted proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`. This changes no Orbit or Eon contract, protocol, endpoint identity, Session lifetime, or single-client rule.

Consumer: a local user who keeps Venus open in standalone or Eon workspace mode. Trigger: the configured standalone endpoint, or the authoritative selected Eon endpoint while its pane remains `live=true`, has no live Venus transport because initial local connection failed or an established attachment ended through EOF or retryable socket I/O. Result: Venus preserves the last coherent accepted presentation, retries that exact endpoint on a bounded schedule, and atomically replaces state with the coherent current Orbit frame after attachment. Important failures: a changed selected endpoint or an authoritative `live=false` selected pane cancels obsolete retry state; explicit Busy, Incompatible, Exited, invalid protocol/model/frame, queue-overflow, invalid-input, and worker-start failures remain terminal and visible rather than creating a retry loop.

The user's 2026-08-10 direction explicitly approves planning this automatic same-endpoint recovery outcome. Update the canonical contract index before implementation and stop if evidence requires a new contract ID or changes the stated failure classification.

## Evidence and minimum shape

- `src/main.rs::handle_transport` clears a terminal transport after loss and has no later attachment trigger. `switch_orbit_endpoint` can already restart a missing same endpoint, but `ven-c87.1` correctly invokes it only for authoritative snapshot-content changes.
- `Application` already owns the selected endpoint, Orbit transport replacement, and winit deadlines; `about_to_wait` already composes `ControlFlow::WaitUntil`. The minimum owner is one application-held retry deadline/backoff state using `std::time`, not Eon inspection and not another worker or module.
- `SessionModel::prepare_reconnect` already resets the frame reducer while retaining the last coherent scene. `Transport::start` already owns one transient attachment attempt and reports its outcome through the event loop.
- EONW's accepted selected-pane `live` value remains authoritative in workspace mode. It gates retry eligibility but does not schedule retries; a liveness change may cancel or re-enter the existing changed-snapshot endpoint path, while an unchanged snapshot still performs no Orbit work.
- Exact Orbit proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757` guarantees one local presentation client, deterministic Busy/Incompatible negotiation, coherent complete state on reattachment, and bounded release after broken clients.

Minimum proposed schedule: retryable loss schedules 250 ms, then doubles through 500 ms, 1 s, and 2 s, capped at 5 s until attachment, endpoint replacement, or application exit. No jitter is needed for one local client. A successful `Attached` cancels the pending retry because a transport is live, and a selected-endpoint change resets the schedule. Recovery is not presentation-complete until the first accepted complete frame from that attachment; retained pre-loss scene data must remain visibly stale until then. During backoff Venus retains the exact bounded loss, and during negotiation or the wait for a fresh frame it reports the existing connecting/waiting state.

Required before code: the complete Bead and comments; `VEN-C3`, `VEN-C4`, and preserved `VEN-C8`; current `src/main.rs`, `src/model.rs`, `src/transport.rs`, their lifecycle tests and direct call sites; exact Orbit session protocol, accept loop, reattachment/lifecycle checks, and canonical proof above; locked winit 0.30.13 `ControlFlow::WaitUntil` behavior routed through `docs/REFERENCES.md`. Comparison only: Orbit's internal canonical presentation-client retry loop. Rejected scope: using periodic EONW `Inspect`, retrying terminal protocol/state failures, changing Orbit, restarting Sessions, configurable timing, jitter, a daemon, a new dependency, a new module, persistence, remote transport, or compatibility behavior.

Platform classification: neutral policy and time math with the existing isolated platform event-loop and local-socket owners. The same winit deadline owner is available on macOS; Unix transport implementation and native proof remain separate platform work. No new macOS blocker is introduced.

## Scope

- Classify retryable local connection/EOF/read/write loss separately from terminal protocol, model, resource-bound, negotiation, process-exit, and worker-start failures at the existing transport/application boundary.
- In workspace mode, require the current accepted selected pane to remain `live=true`; cancel retry when Eon changes the selected endpoint or marks that pane non-live. Standalone mode uses its configured endpoint without inventing an Eon liveness signal.
- Schedule, start, reset, and cancel same-endpoint attachment attempts in the application lifecycle owner.
- Preserve the last accepted scene during loss and backoff; accept only a fresh coherent Orbit attachment/frame through the existing reducer.
- Keep input gated while detached, preserve exact focus/resize replay after attachment, and avoid duplicate transports or stale endpoint attempts.
- Cover standalone and Eon workspace launches, including a Venus-before-Orbit startup race.
- Update `VEN-C3` and `VEN-C4` in the contract index before implementation, preserve their prior immutable proof as historical evidence while the change is a candidate, and advance proof only at an accepted commit. Update current-state README and changelog only for accepted behavior, plus exact LOC accounting.

Out of scope: Eon polling or protocol changes; retries after Busy, Incompatible, Exited, invalid ORBS/model/frame, bounded queue overflow, invalid local input, or thread-spawn failure; Orbit/Session restart ownership; user-configurable policy; background services; remote transport; dependency or module additions.

## Acceptance

1. After a retryable initial connection failure or established socket loss, Venus attempts only the configured standalone endpoint or the still-selected authoritative Eon endpoint while its pane remains `live=true`, on the declared bounded schedule, with no busy spin, parallel attempt, or use of periodic Eon snapshots as a retry clock.
2. If that endpoint becomes available, Venus attaches without user input, cancels pending retry, receives one coherent complete current frame, replays the latest resize and focus through existing semantics, and replaces the stale scene only through the canonical reducer. `Attached` alone does not mark retained pre-loss scene data current or clear the waiting-for-current-frame indication.
3. During backoff, Venus retains the last complete scene and exact bounded loss status; an active attempt shows Connecting, and an attached transport without its first fresh frame remains explicitly waiting. Input remains gated until `Attached`.
4. Selecting a different Eon endpoint or receiving authoritative `live=false` for the selected pane cancels obsolete retry state. A later changed snapshot restoring a live selected endpoint follows the existing endpoint path. Unchanged workspace snapshots cause no redraw, accessibility update, endpoint reconciliation, or retry.
5. Busy, Incompatible, Exited, invalid protocol/model/frame, queue-overflow, invalid-input, and worker-start failures remain explicit terminal states and do not reconnect automatically.
6. Deterministic model/application checks prove delay progression and cap, cancellation after attachment, reset after endpoint replacement, stale or non-live workspace endpoint cancellation, retryable-versus-terminal classification, one attempt at a time, same-endpoint recovery, retained-scene stale marking until the first fresh frame, and unchanged-workspace isolation without wall-clock sleeps.
7. Transport integration checks prove a missing startup socket later attaches and an established dropped local connection reattaches, while dropping Venus cancels pending work and leaks no thread.
8. Native Linux dogfood starts Venus before Orbit, observes automatic attachment after Orbit appears, then exercises one same-path loss/reavailability cycle and confirms recovery without clicking, focusing, changing Eon topology, or restarting Venus.
9. The locked Rust verification suite and `git diff --check` pass. Proof records exact Venus, Orbit, executable, environment, timing observations, and remaining platform gaps.

## Sequencing

- Depends on `ven-c87.1`, because that active frontier changes the same workspace/transport/model owner flow and establishes the invariant that Eon refresh does not own Orbit recovery.
- Must complete before the transport/model, host-lifecycle, input/effects, accessibility, and scene/renderer subsystem audits, because their scopes cover attachment state, focus/resize replay, status exposure, or retained-scene presentation. Their existing dependencies then hold the cross-subsystem integration audit until the complete accepted state has been reviewed.

title: Use a supported wgpu surface alpha mode
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens the existing `VEN-C1` native presentation boundary and preserves `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C4`, `VEN-C7`, and `VEN-C8`; it adds or changes no product contract. The correction uses the already selected wgpu 30.0.0 surface-configuration owner and requires no dependency or wire change.

Deferred while another issue owns the one active cross-repository implementation frontier.

## Why

Consumer: a local user starting Venus on any surface accepted by the selected wgpu adapter.

Trigger: wgpu reports a valid surface whose supported composite-alpha list contains `Inherit` but not `Opaque`.

Result: Venus configures the surface with a mode supported by its reported capabilities and retains an opaque terminal presentation through its normal clear/draw path.

Important failure: do not reject a valid WSI surface by overriding wgpu's supported default with an unsupported explicit alpha mode.

Audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` found this at Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`. Impact MED. Effort S. Implementation risk LOW. Confidence HIGH in the API mismatch and MED in occurrence on currently exercised targets.

## Evidence

- `src/render.rs:193-207`: Renderer begins with `Surface::get_default_config`, then unconditionally replaces `CompositeAlphaMode::Auto` with `Opaque`.
- wgpu-types 30.0.0 `src/surface.rs:504-529`: `SurfaceCapabilities::alpha_modes` guarantees at least one of `Opaque` or `Inherit`, not `Opaque` specifically.
- wgpu 30.0.0 `src/api/surface.rs:83-100`: the default configuration uses `Auto`.
- wgpu-core 30.0.0 `src/device/surface_config.rs:137-173`: `Auto` chooses a supported Opaque/Inherit fallback, while an unsupported explicit value produces `UnsupportedAlphaMode`.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/render.rs` surface configuration during initialization and any shared recovery/resizing use of the stored configuration.
- The cheapest proof that Venus does not choose an unsupported alpha mode.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof metadata for preserved/hardened contracts after a committed source candidate, README LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG only if the accepted correction is consumer-visible.

Out of scope:
- Transparent windows, compositor effects, opacity configuration, HDR/color-space policy, renderer replacement, another backend, macOS support promises, or dependencies.
- A custom alpha-selection abstraction when retaining wgpu's supported default is sufficient.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- This Bead and audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db`.

title: Render interruptible kinetic touchpad scrolling
description:
## Contract routing

Change proved VEN-C7 and preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C8, VEN-C9, and VEN-C13. Consume the revised ORB-C8 preview and typed-wheel outcome through canonical ORBS v4 only after eon-sessions issue orb-orbit-typed-wheel-outcomes-5nq has an accepted proof commit. Orbit remains the sole owner of terminal modes, PTY input, retained history, viewport position, clamps, and complete frames. Venus owns native gesture collection, transient presentation offset, release velocity, animation deadlines, and bounded client-visible failure.

Consumer: a local user scrolling an Orbit-backed terminal with a touchpad in Venus.

Trigger: winit 0.30.13 delivers a continuous PixelDelta wheel sequence with reliable Started, Moved, and Ended or Cancelled phases over the terminal surface.

Result: terminal content follows the finger in pixel increments using the current authoritative scene plus one revision-bound adjacent row. Ended continues the measured motion with monotonic deceleration until rest or an Orbit clamp. A new Started cancels active inertia before applying the physical delta, so touching the pad immediately takes control. Cancelled launches no inertia and settles to the nearest valid row. LineDelta and phase-incomplete platform streams retain the current bounded whole-row behavior.

Important failures: terminal mouse tracking and alternate-screen DEC 1007 keep their exact input behavior with no client animation. A fresh Orbit frame invalidates a stale preview. Transport pressure, loss, resize, focus loss, selection, another semantic input, or endpoint change removes transient motion without blank rows, stale presentation, hidden input, unbounded requests, or a Venus history owner.

## Chosen shape

Use the existing winit, event loop, renderer, scene, input state, model, and transport. Add no crate and no Venus module.

- Feed MouseWheel.phase into the terminal wheel path instead of discarding it.
- Apply direct manipulation only after a PixelDelta stream demonstrates a reliable phase lifecycle. Keep LineDelta and Moved-only input on current cell-normalized accumulation.
- When direction becomes known, request one Orbit preview against the exact presented frame revision. Accumulate physical deltas while it is in flight. A terminal-routed response keeps discrete accumulation and sends an actual wheel only at the existing cell threshold. A viewport response supplies zero or one adjacent row without moving authority.
- Materialize only the current accepted scene and that adjacent row. Translate and clip the scene by a fractional cell-height offset and draw the row at the entering edge. The offset cannot cross a full row until the actual wheel result arrives.
- Commit an actual wheel step only when motion or release snapping reaches a row boundary. The typed Orbit outcome either installs the new authoritative frame and resets the fractional origin, reports a clamp, or reports that terminal state changed and routed input. Discard the preview after any outcome.
- For continued motion, request the next adjacent row from the new exact revision. Keep at most one preview or wheel request in flight.
- Estimate release velocity from a small bounded window of monotonic timestamped samples. Advance one deterministic time-based friction curve through the existing host deadline owner. Bound elapsed time and velocity, stop below one threshold, and settle to the nearest row without a discontinuous jump.
- A new Started clears velocity and the inertial deadline synchronously, then lets the new gesture control the current fractional position. Cancelled settles without using release velocity.
- Clear transient state before resize, scene replacement, endpoint replacement, reconnect, selection, focus loss, or other semantic input can make the base revision stale.

No configuration knob is part of the first slice. Tune one fixed curve and snap rule through native dogfood; record their constants and environment.

Impact: HIGH because this changes the feel of every touchpad history interaction.
Effort: L, roughly 300-550 owned production and focused test lines if one adjacent row is sufficient.
Risk: HIGH because platform phases, protocol latency, snapping, and renderer clipping meet at this boundary.
Portability: isolated platform dependency. Linux Wayland is the required proof target. X11 and phase-incomplete streams keep discrete behavior. macOS remains unproved and must not receive client-generated inertia without checking native momentum.

## Reference classification

Required before code:

- The complete issue and accepted proof from orb-orbit-typed-wheel-outcomes-5nq.
- Current Venus src/input.rs, src/main.rs, src/model.rs, src/transport.rs, src/scene.rs, src/render.rs, docs/CONTRACTS.md, and docs/REFERENCES.md.
- Wayland wl_pointer version 10. Finger-axis motion is continuous surface-space input, clients may transform content by that distance, and axis_stop after finger lift enables kinetic scrolling: https://wayland.app/protocols/wayland
- winit 0.30.13 WindowEvent::MouseWheel, MouseScrollDelta, TouchPhase, and its Wayland mapping of non-discrete axes to PixelDelta and axis_stop to Ended: https://docs.rs/winit/0.30.13/winit/event/enum.WindowEvent.html
- Official libinput scroll-source guidance. Finger-source callers own velocity, friction, and cancellation; wheel input remains immediate: https://wayland.freedesktop.org/libinput/doc/0.0/scrolling.html

Comparison only:

- GTK 4 EventControllerScroll. It encloses continuous deltas in begin/end and can report end velocity through decelerate: https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.EventControllerScroll.html
- Ghostty commit 45db2c2551ecc016f9746e8e2855f4f8a3871e7b under MIT. Its precision path accumulates pixels into rows. Keep the wheel/precision distinction; reject its GTK widgets, same-process authority, multiplier setting, and renderer.
- Rio commit 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 under MIT. Its integer display offset does not solve direct pixel presentation across Orbit.
- WezTerm commit 577474d89ee61aef4a48145cdec82a638d874751 for stable and viewport-adjacent rows. Reject its general cache and lazy history plane.
- Apple NSEvent phase and momentumPhase are conditional on approved macOS work. AppKit emits its own dissipating momentum stream, while winit maps physical and momentum phases into one TouchPhase surface; Venus must not double inertia: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsevent/momentumphase

No source reuse or dependency is selected.

## Scope and sequence

1. Wait for the exact accepted Orbit proof and update the one canonical protocol import; no compatibility adapter.
2. Write one deterministic gesture-state check first using pixel deltas, phases, timestamps, base revisions, preview rows, typed wheel outcomes, and frame invalidation.
3. Add the smallest input state and current-scene-plus-edge-row renderer path.
4. Drive animation through the existing event-loop deadline and redraw owners.
5. Dogfood on a real Linux Wayland touchpad with deep history, live bottom, top clamp, slow partial pull, fast flick, reversal, a fresh touch during inertia, a cancellation, terminal mouse tracking, DEC 1007, resize, selection, and reconnect.
6. Update VEN-C7, exact Orbit proof metadata, references, README LOC, and changelog only after an accepted proof-bearing source commit.
7. Create or activate a separate Eon/Eonova runtime-acceptance issue only after the Venus proof exists.

## Acceptance

1. After the bounded local preview arrives, rendered content tracks PixelDelta motion at fractional row offsets. The entering edge contains the exact adjacent Orbit row; no blank strip, duplicate row, stale glyph, or client-invented cell appears.
2. A partial low-velocity release settles smoothly to the nearest row. Returning to the current row emits no wheel. Completing the adjacent row emits exactly one wheel and installs its typed authoritative result.
3. Ended launches time-based deceleration from bounded recent samples. Speed decreases monotonically and is redraw-cadence independent within recorded tolerance.
4. A new Started during inertia cancels the prior velocity and deadline before the next inertial step, then immediately controls the current fractional position. Cancelled uses no release velocity.
5. At most one preview or wheel request is in flight, one adjacent row is retained, and the offset never outruns available authoritative presentation. Queue pressure cannot grow with gesture duration or frame rate.
6. An absent adjacent row or applied row zero stops at the exact top or bottom with no overscroll. Reversal remains coherent and replaces only the direction-bound preview.
7. Terminal-routed preview uses current discrete accumulation; actual terminal mouse and DEC 1007 bytes remain exact. A route change at commit cancels visual motion and cannot invent a viewport step.
8. Any newer ordinary frame, resize, selection, focus loss, other input, reconnect, endpoint change, failure, or exit invalidates the preview and clears the fractional offset.
9. Focused checks cover start/move/end/cancel, preview latency, low and high velocity, cadence variation, snapping, fresh-touch interruption, reversal, clamps, route change, stale revision, queue bounds, and every cancellation surface. Renderer proof covers edge-row translation and clipping.
10. Native Linux Wayland dogfood records compositor, winit version, hardware, scale, preview latency, frame timing, curve and snap constants, and user acceptance.
11. Locked Rust checks, Clippy, diff check, LOC accounting, exact contract proof update, and Beads flush pass.

## Non-goals and stop conditions

No bounce, elastic overscroll, scrollbar, general animation framework, shader, setting, gesture library, new dependency, arbitrary history cache, speculative macOS backend, X11 inertia promise, or terminal-mode inference in Venus.

Stop before code until the user approves the VEN-C7 change and the exact Orbit proof is available. Stop if winit does not deliver reliable Started/Ended PixelDelta on the target Wayland compositor; changing the window backend or adding GTK requires a new decision. Stop if one adjacent row cannot keep the surface complete or the measured preview latency makes direct manipulation visibly lag; return that gap to Orbit instead of caching history. Stop if another active issue owns src/render.rs, src/model.rs, src/input.rs, or the protocol import.

title: Request compositor-owned background blur
description:
## Contract routing

This issue proposes new product contract `VEN-C15`: compositor-owned background blur requests for one Venus surface. Before any production, test, manifest, or generated edit, the executing agent must obtain user approval for the exact contract text and index it in `docs/CONTRACTS.md`. It preserves `VEN-C1` through `VEN-C14`, canonical ORBS v3 at `orbit-protocol` revision `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`, and EONW v1 at `eon-workspace-protocol` revision `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`. Orbit and Eon workspace protocols remain unchanged.

The user selected Plan A on 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo: retain winit, temporarily pin the exact v0.30.13 backport of `ext-background-effect-v1`, and prove native COSMIC Wayland behavior. This planning decision does not waive the repository contract, reference, or crate gates.

Candidate observable contract:

- Consumer: Eon, EonTerm, or a direct caller launching one Venus surface.
- Trigger: launch with `--background-blur`; absence preserves the current no-blur request.
- Result: Venus asks the selected native window backend for full-surface background blur before showing the window. On the required COSMIC Wayland proof target, winit selects `ext-background-effect-v1`; translucent terminal-default pixels reveal compositor blur while explicit cell backgrounds, selection, inverse video, workspace chrome, notices, focus borders, text, cursor, input, IME, and accessibility remain unchanged.
- Limits and failures: Venus does not own blur radius, strength, algorithm, or compositor policy. The selected winit API does not expose compositor capability or acceptance, so non-COSMIC compositors are a best-effort request rather than a visible-blur guarantee. X11 and macOS behavior are unproved. Launch parsing retains current bounded rejection of unknown or excess arguments.

Impact: MED/HIGH visible product value. Effort: M including dependency gate and native proof. Implementation risk: MED because the source pin affects the full native host even though the Venus code change is small. Confidence: HIGH for COSMIC Wayland and dependency fit.

## Evidence

- `Cargo.toml:16` pins crates.io winit 0.30.13 with X11, Wayland, dynamic Wayland loading, and raw-window-handle 0.6.
- `src/main.rs:184-217` owns pre-show window attributes, transparency, AccessKit creation, renderer creation, IME enablement, and visibility. Blur belongs on this existing creation boundary.
- `README.md:149-158` currently excludes blur and names winit as the native host.
- `docs/CRATES.md:15` makes winit the sole window, event-loop, native input, IME, resize, recovery, and scheduling owner; replacing or bypassing it would duplicate that boundary.
- Closed `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` proves `VEN-C11` background opacity and explicitly stopped before blur. Its accepted layer policy already makes translucent terminal-default pixels and opaque explicit/workspace layers deterministic.
- Exact winit 0.30.13 documents Wayland blur only through `org_kde_kwin_blur_manager`, which does not satisfy COSMIC.
- winit PR 4580 commit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08` is exactly one commit above tag v0.30.13 and backports upstream merged, verified commit `c4afadbfabf7b1e7989b40b493db1a4c7bd8ff4e`. It prefers `ext-background-effect-v1`, retains the KDE fallback, and changes 200 additions / 30 deletions across eight winit files without changing the public blur API.
- The original upstream PR 4553 passed its complete CI matrix. The backport stable and nightly Wayland jobs pass; its red aggregate includes unrelated current Clippy, dependency-MSRV, and cargo-deny drift. The backport has no peer review or automated compositor integration test.
- A disposable Venus evaluation at HEAD `27af57690cf79b1f4a04b6a71eeb17cd05c9b3e1` applied `[patch.crates-io]` at exact `fb45fbf`, resolved one shared winit through `accesskit_winit`, and passed `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, 46 library + 19 host + 12 canonical tests, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`. The lock source changed winit and the workspace `dpi` package from crates.io 0.1.2 to exact fork revision 0.1.1; no second winit was introduced.
- Installed COSMIC compositor 1.0.0 at exact commit `091583ac84abac02967ae358cf9570ddfef63b31`, as well as current upstream `3b8bac8335ed017a70f1ffe865c86d1ffe07c0cb`, implements Smithay `ExtBackgroundEffectHandler`, advertises `Capability::Blur`, and applies a surface-local blur region.
- `ext-background-effect-v1` version 1 defines a compositor capability event and a double-buffered, surface-local blur region; the algorithm remains compositor policy.
- An all-status Beads search found no existing blur implementation issue. The typography issue mentions blur only as excluded scope.

## Scope

In scope:

- Candidate `VEN-C15` contract indexing and proof metadata.
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`: keep the existing exact winit dependency and use `[patch.crates-io]` for `https://github.com/chiyuki0325/winit-0.30.git` at exact revision `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`.
- `src/main.rs`: one bounded launch boolean and `WindowAttributes::with_blur` before window creation.
- Existing launch tests and the cheapest checks proving default parity and requested blur plumbing.
- `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, README current-state behavior and LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG for accepted visible behavior.
- Native COSMIC Wayland proof with compositor frosted-window policy enabled, standalone and Eon workspace surfaces, existing background opacity, decorations, and resize.

Out of scope:

- Blur radius, strength, algorithm, per-cell or configurable regions, live toggling/reload, background images, click-through, shaders, offscreen passes, or renderer changes.
- A Venus Wayland protocol module, direct `wayland-client` ownership, unsafe code, winit replacement, SDL, Tao, GTK, libcosmic, or a new event loop.
- Eon persistence/schema/defaults and Nova/Yazelix mapping; create their independently reviewable consumer issues only after the Venus contract and source proof are accepted.
- Orbit or EONW fields, compatibility adapters, arbitrary split layout, X11 blur guarantees, or macOS implementation/proof.
- Compositor configuration UI or a promise that every compositor applies the request.

## Reference and crate gate

Required before code:

- Current `AGENTS.md`; this issue and all comments; `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`; current `VEN-C1`, `VEN-C9`, `VEN-C11`, and `VEN-C14` owners and checks.
- Complete current launch parsing, window creation, transparency, renderer surface setup/recovery, AccessKit, input/IME, workspace layering, and relevant tests.
- Exact crates.io winit 0.30.13 source and exact fork commit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`; exact upstream source commit `c4afadbfabf7b1e7989b40b493db1a4c7bd8ff4e`; PR 4580 and upstream PR 4553 histories and CI.
- Exact `wayland-protocols` 1.46 `ext-background-effect-v1` specification (the first corrected release) and the byte-identical locked Rust crate generation at 0.32.13. Release 1.45 is rejected because its blur capability value is the incompatible zero encoding.
- Exact COSMIC compositor source at installed proof commit `091583ac84abac02967ae358cf9570ddfef63b31`; current upstream comparison only if the installed implementation differs.
- Existing accepted Eon launch boundary only to preserve update order; no Eon edit belongs to this issue.

Conditional:

- KDE protocol behavior only if regression proof is extended beyond COSMIC.
- A newer stable winit release only if it contains the same upstream mechanism before implementation begins; if so, rerun the crate gate and prefer crates.io.
- Non-COSMIC compositor sources only after a named native failure or user-selected portability expansion.

Rejected:

- Direct protocol plumbing around winit, replacing winit, SDL3, Tao/GTK, a generic presentation profile, a blur amount, or a second window owner. These add ownership without improving the selected COSMIC contract.

License and dependency disposition:

- winit and the fork retain the upstream Apache-2.0 license; COSMIC compositor source is evidence only and is not copied or incorporated.
- Before manifest edits, append a `Crate gate` comment comparing exact sources, 200/30 upstream delta, direct/transitive/native/build/Nix cost, the git-sourced `dpi` change, Linux/COSMIC behavior, macOS feasibility, input/IME/accessibility preservation, upgrade burden, and replacement cost. Stop for user approval as required by repository policy.
- Exit condition: replace the fork patch with the first accepted stable crates.io winit release containing the upstream mechanism, rerun all native-host proofs touched by the upgrade, and remove fork-specific documentation.

Platform disposition: isolated platform dependency. COSMIC Wayland is required proof. Existing X11 behavior without the new flag remains preserved; macOS remains architecturally credible but unproved.

## Implementation notes

1. Reconfirm the one active cross-repository frontier and that no issue owns `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, or the window-creation path. Obtain approval for the exact `VEN-C15` contract and index it before implementation.
2. Claim this issue and append the required Execution baseline with current HEAD, AGENTS hash, issue revision, contracts, exact Orbit/Eon proofs, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and agent identity.
3. Complete the required reference gate. Then append the crate matrix and stop for dependency approval before manifest edits.
4. Keep `winit = "=0.30.13"` as the dependency contract and add only the exact `[patch.crates-io]` revision. Update the lock deterministically. Require `cargo tree -i winit -e normal` to show one winit shared by Venus and `accesskit_winit`; inspect the exact `dpi` source change.
5. Extend the existing launch parser and `Application` state with one boolean. Apply `.with_blur(background_blur)` on the existing pre-creation attributes. Add no module, adapter, capability cache, or platform abstraction.
6. Test no-flag parity, flag parsing, bounded invalid arguments, and that the selected creation attributes receive the boolean through the smallest deterministic seam. Do not test winit internals.
7. On exact COSMIC Wayland with frosted-window policy enabled, compare flag off/on over a visually discriminating background at opacity 0.88 and 0.0. Cover standalone/workspace, decorated/undecorated creation, resize, active Orbit background changes, opaque explicit cells/selection/inverse/workspace chrome, cursor/text/IME/input/accessibility, reconnect, and bounded loss notice.
8. Commit and verify the source candidate first. Then advance contract and crate metadata, README LOC, accepted changelog text, and issue closure against that source commit in the required follow-up commit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The exact approved `VEN-C15` row states request semantics, COSMIC proof scope, compositor-owned policy, and the lack of portable capability reporting without widening `VEN-C11`.
2. No flag produces byte-for-byte-equivalent launch configuration and current accepted rendering/input/accessibility behavior.
3. `--background-blur` is accepted exactly once through the existing parser and requests blur before the hidden window becomes visible. Unknown and excess arguments retain bounded failure.
4. Blur does not modify scene colors, alpha, draw inputs, surface blend modes, render pipelines, or workspace layer ownership. At opacity 1.0 it may be visually occluded; the flag remains independent rather than inventing coupling.
5. Cargo resolves one exact winit shared with `accesskit_winit`, records fork revision `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08`, and contains only reviewed expected lock changes including git workspace `dpi` 0.1.1.
6. Native COSMIC Wayland visibly distinguishes blur off from on at opacity 0.88 and 0.0. Standalone and workspace terminal areas blur while opaque explicit cells, selection/inverse, workspace chrome, notices, focus borders, text, and cursor retain their accepted appearance.
7. Decorations, resize, dynamic terminal background changes, IME, keyboard, pointer, selection, accessibility, reconnect, and failure presentation preserve current contracts.
8. Unsupported or policy-disabled compositors are documented as best effort; Venus makes no false guarantee or owned blur-algorithm claim.
9. The locked Rust suite, focused tests, dependency tree check, diff check, LOC accounting, exact proof metadata, and Beads flush pass on one materially unchanged candidate.
10. Closure records exact winit/fork/upstream/COSMIC/protocol identities, commands, test counts, native environment and policy, observations, lock delta, license disposition, proof limits, and the stable-release exit condition.

## Verification

- Focused launch tests for default and `--background-blur` behavior should fail before and pass after implementation.
- `cargo tree -i winit -e normal` should show exactly one winit used by Venus and `accesskit_winit`.
- `cargo tree -p winit --depth 2` and reviewed `Cargo.lock` diff should match the accepted crate gate.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br sync --flush-only`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged source candidate. Native proof must name COSMIC version/commit, Wayland rather than Xwayland, frosted-window policy, GPU/backend, opacity, and observed scope.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until the exact new contract is user-approved and indexed.
- Stop before manifest edits until the crate gate is recorded and the dependency change is approved.
- Stop if stable winit already contains the mechanism; prefer the stable release through a fresh gate instead of retaining the fork.
- Stop if the fork revision is unavailable, differs from the reviewed one-commit v0.30.13 delta, introduces a second winit, or changes dependencies beyond the reviewed `dpi` source/version.
- Stop if COSMIC at the exact proof revision does not advertise and visibly apply `Capability::Blur`, or if correct output requires renderer, shader, surface-alpha, or compositor-setting ownership changes.
- Stop if implementation requires direct Wayland registry/event-queue access, unsafe code, another module, another event loop, winit replacement, a public capability guarantee, or an Eon/Orbit protocol change.
- Stop if another active issue owns the launch parser, window lifecycle, manifest, lockfile, opacity owner, AccessKit adapter, or renderer surface setup.
- Stop rather than adding Eon persistence, Nova mapping, blur strength, live reload, X11 guarantees, or macOS proof.

## Maintenance notes

The invariant is deliberately small: Venus owns one boolean request at its existing native-window boundary; winit owns protocol selection and lifecycle; COSMIC owns the visual algorithm and policy; Eon may later own persistence and defaults. The cheapest removal path is deleting the patch when stable winit carries upstream commit `c4afadbf`.

The selected patch is preferable to direct Wayland code because it preserves one native-host owner and one AccessKit-compatible winit instance. Reconsider replacing winit only after multiple independently required native protocols are blocked and upstream extension is no longer viable.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted VEN-C15 at source proof 7fc7e4ba97aaf48b586002934a580ef2d1c31694; exact locked checks and native COSMIC Wayland dogfood pass.

title: Expose a Venus-native target from Yazelix Cursors
description:
## Outcome and boundary

Consumer: Eon at launch time.

Trigger: Eon resolves the active Yazelix Cursors configuration for a Venus window.

Result: the child library returns one typed, versioned native cursor presentation containing only `tail` or `none`, one resolved trail color, and the duration multiplier. For both mono and split definitions, this target projects the first resolved palette color; Eon and Venus never receive family, accent, secondary color, divider, transition, or cursor-color override data. Orbit-authored cursor color remains unchanged. Yazelix Cursors remains the sole owner of preset lookup, palette lookup, target projection, validation, and random selection.

Important failures: an unknown preset or palette, malformed color, invalid duration, or explicit unsupported movement effect returns a bounded child-owned error. Eon and Venus must not parse the child configuration, duplicate its registry, infer unsupported effects, or consume generated Ghostty shaders.

This tracker owns the work because `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/cursors` has no Beads store. Implementation belongs only in that repository. This issue changes no `VEN-C*`, `EON-C*`, Orbit protocol, Eon workspace protocol, or Venus source.

## Evidence and decision

The user accepted the narrow consumption boundary on 2026-08-11 America/Sao_Paulo. Exact inspected child revision: `e0f8bc9492dbfaaf498cef47d543010f4abb2b8f`. `CursorRegistry`, `CursorSettings`, `CursorDefinition`, and `ResolvedCursorRegistryState` already own configuration and selected registry values. `CURSOR_TARGET_CONTRACTS` already documents consumer-specific targets, but no Eon/Venus target exists. The Rio target describes a shader ABI and is not the native Venus contract.

Adopt the existing registry, resolver, target-contract table, error style, and CLI target validation. Reject a second schema, Eon-owned preset interpretation, a subprocess boundary, generated shader reuse, a general capability-negotiation system, and copying the 3,331-line child into Eon. Apache-2.0 remains compatible with direct exact-revision dependency use; preserve notices.

## Minimum scope

- Add one explicit `eon-venus-native-v1` target contract.
- Add the smallest typed output and resolver needed by an exact-revision Rust consumer: `None` or `Tail { color, duration }`. Reuse the existing registry selection, first resolved palette color, duration, and errors.
- Project both mono and split definitions to `colors[0]` inside Yazelix Cursors. Do not expose a palette, family, accent, secondary color, split metadata, or cursor-color override through v1.
- Resolve `trail_effect = random` only across effects supported by this target; with the v1 set it resolves to `tail`. Accept explicit `tail` and `none`. Reject explicit `warp`, `sweep`, or any later unsupported movement effect with a target-specific error.
- Treat mode-change effects, glow, shader uniforms, and shader file generation as outside this target. The target documentation must not imply that Venus consumes them.
- Preserve all existing Ghostty, Rio-compatible-config, Mars, Ratty, and protocol-position target behavior.
- Update current README/API documentation and the existing focused registry, resolver, CLI, and target-contract tests.

Out of scope: Eon persistence or defaults, Eon launch policy, Venus CLI encoding, spring physics, GPU drawing, cursor-color override, multiple trail colors, arbitrary shaders, live reload, a new config format, a new dependency, or target discovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One child-owned API returns a versioned native presentation with only `None` or `Tail { color, duration }`; the color is exactly the selected definition`s first resolved palette color.
- Existing preset and palette validation remains the source of truth. No consumer must reconstruct registry rules.
- `tail`, `none`, target-scoped effect `random`, mono projection, split first-color projection, and the shipped default have deterministic tests. Unsupported explicit movement effects fail with a stable bounded error.
- The default shipped configuration resolves successfully for the native target.
- Target metadata and CLI validation report the v1 capability without claiming mode effects, glow, shader ABI, or generated assets.
- Existing target output and tests remain unchanged.
- README states the ownership split and exact unsupported fields in present tense.

## Verification

Use TDD at the resolver boundary. Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --locked`, `nix build`, `nix run .#yzc -- --help`, focused target validation, and `git diff --check`. Record the exact source revision and API surface for the Eon and Venus follow-ups.

## Stop conditions

Stop for user approval before changing the global config schema, adding a dependency, exposing shader files or uniforms to Eon/Venus, supporting another movement effect, moving persistence into the child, or adding a compatibility window. Stop if the current resolver cannot express the target without duplicating registry state; revise the child owner instead of pushing interpretation downstream.

## Maintenance

The v1 removal path is one target contract, one single-color typed projection, and focused tests. A later multi-color target requires an explicitly versioned contract after Venus proves a named need; v1 never grows palette semantics in place.
